clue.text: Standard to aim for on course

definitions.meaning: a standard is a banner or ensign carried aloft
on a golf course the marker pole in the hole is what a player aims at

explanation.surface: A golfer describes the usual target to head for on the links.
explanation.definitionFit: A banner is a standard, and the pennant on its pole marks each hole that golfers play towards.

clue.text: Reckoned using buff coloured dice?

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast, a fan

indicators.note: coloured means the letters of dice are distorted into a new order

explanation.surface: A gambler calculates the odds using tan-tinted dice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buff' looks like a colour but is an enthusiast; 'coloured' rearranges DICE into CIED. 'using' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy that something is so is to think or suppose it.

clue.text: Order from the highest level

definitions.meaning: a classical architectural style of column, from ancient Athens
the room at the very top of a house, under the roof

explanation.surface: A command comes down from the top floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link. In architecture an order is a column style; this one is a square-pillared Greek variant.
explanation.definitionFit: Names both a Greek column style and the top storey under the roof.

clue.text: Send out to get great physician back

indicators.note: back tells us the word for the great physician is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: from the saying that time is a great healer

explanation.surface: Someone is dispatched to fetch back an eminent doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TIME (the proverbial great healer) to give the answer; 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To give off or discharge is to send out, as a lamp sends out light.

clue.text: Moderate means

definitions.meaning: a channel or agency through which something is done

explanation.surface: Modest resources.
explanation.definitionFit: It means average in size, and also a channel of communication.

clue.text: Panel receives gold cross for displays

indicators.note: receives means the panel word takes on the following pieces

parts.note: a table is a flat panel or slab
AU is the chemical symbol for gold
X is a cross

explanation.surface: A board is awarded a gold cross for its exhibits.
explanation.definitionFit: Staged scenes or pictorial groupings are displays.

clue.text: Get into gear in a Mini, perhaps

definitions.meaning: to put on one's clothes, gear being clothing
a mini is a short skirted garment, one example of the type

explanation.surface: A driver shifts into gear in a small British car.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mini looks like the famous small British car; here it is a miniskirt-length frock.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting on clothes is to clothe oneself, and a mini is a short frock.

clue.text: Young women gained, relatively speaking, by union

definitions.text: Young women gained, relatively speaking, by union

parts.words: Young women gained, relatively speaking, by union
parts.note: the female relatives who come to parents when a son marries

explanation.surface: Girls acquired as relatives through a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A son's wife is a parent's relation through marriage, gained when the couple wed.

clue.text: Arms are essential for this engagement

definitions.text: Arms are essential for this engagement

parts.words: Arms are essential for this engagement
parts.note: sounds military, but the arms are limbs used to hug someone

explanation.surface: Weapons are needed for this battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arms' and 'engagement' suggest war; it is a hug.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugging somebody uses the arms, a close engagement.

clue.text: List points raised for politician

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the pieces are read upwards

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties
N, E and S are compass points

explanation.surface: A list of talking points is brought up for a legislator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns ROTANES upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a senate is a legislator.

clue.text: Description of bishop's moving for all equally

definitions.meaning: in chess the bishop travels diagonally over the chequered playing surface

explanation.surface: A churchman's progress is described as fair to everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Means applying universally, and literally describes a chess bishop's diagonal travel.

clue.text: Marked above zero?

definitions.meaning: above freezing point, water is not frozen

explanation.surface: A thermometer or a grade sheet shows a score just over nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To mark something is to observe it; and above freezing, water is not frozen solid.

clue.text: Spirit of the House

definitions.meaning: an American whiskey distilled mainly from maize
the royal dynasty that ruled France, Spain and Naples

explanation.surface: A ghost haunts the family mansion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link between the two definitions; House here means a royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an American corn whiskey and a European royal dynasty.

clue.text: Popular conclusion that's no longer common?

parts.note: in fashion, popular, is IN
an ending or close is a closure

explanation.surface: A well-liked ending that has become rare.
explanation.walkthrough: Old spelling for land fenced off: common land so taken was no longer common.
explanation.definitionFit: Fencing in common land made it private, so such a field had stopped being shared ground.

clue.text: Try to see time on ticker

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: a judge who tries a case hears it

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to check the time on a watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ticker' looks like a clock but is slang for the organ that beats in your chest; 'to see' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticker is informal slang for the organ that pumps blood.

clue.text: US lawyer to screen material

parts.note: a District Attorney in the US is a DA
to screen is to hide, or mask

explanation.surface: An American attorney wants to keep some evidence hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: A patterned woven fabric, originally from Damascus, used for table linen.

clue.text: Review announced on April Fool's day?

indicators.note: announced signals that the phrase is spoken and heard as a soundalike

parts.note: the first of April comes when the third month has gone by

explanation.surface: An inspection is proclaimed for the first of April.
explanation.walkthrough: A parade of troops before a dignitary sounds like 'March passed', which is true on 1 April.
explanation.definitionFit: A military review is a parade of troops before an inspecting officer.

clue.text: Paramount chief

definitions.meaning: the head of a religious house, as in Mother ___

explanation.surface: Describes a film studio's boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramount means supreme, and the head of a convent or monastery holds that title.

clue.text: Catch opening that may let one down

definitions.text: Catch opening that may let one down

parts.note: to catch is to trap
a door is an opening

explanation.surface: A latch on a hatch might fail.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a hinged floor hatch, and its two parts build it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged floor hatch can drop a person below.

clue.text: Like the territory Darwin grew up in

definitions.text: Like the territory Darwin grew up in

parts.words: Like the territory Darwin grew up in
parts.note: suggests the naturalist's youth, but Darwin is the city that grew in an Australian territory named for its position at the top of the country

explanation.surface: Asks about the land of Charles Darwin's boyhood.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Darwin grew up in Shropshire; the city of Darwin is the capital of Australia's Northern Territory.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian territory containing the city of Darwin is named for lying at the top of the country.

clue.text: Is it ideal for eating chestnuts?

definitions.text: Is it ideal for eating chestnuts?

parts.words: Is it ideal for eating chestnuts?
parts.note: chestnuts are reddish-brown horses, which feed from a sack hung on the head

explanation.surface: Asks about the best way to eat roasted chestnuts.
explanation.walkthrough: A chestnut here is a horse of that colour, fed from a bag strapped over its muzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeding bag fastened over a horse's head holds its fodder.

clue.text: Conventions put years on Uncle Sam

indicators.note: in an across answer the years piece put on another comes after it

parts.note: Uncle Sam personifies the United States, US
a long spell of years is ages

explanation.surface: Customs pile years onto the figure of America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put' is a link; Uncle Sam is the cartoon figure standing for America.
explanation.definitionFit: Customs and established practices are conventions.

clue.text: Had a session about beef problem — it's not really any risk

indicators.note: about means the session word goes around the next piece

parts.note: to sit for a session is to have sat

indicators.note: problem signals that the letters of beef are in disorder

explanation.surface: A meeting over a complaint concludes there's nothing to fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beef' looks like meat but means a complaint, here just letters to shuffle; the rearranged letters sit between the A and T of the session word.
explanation.definitionFit: A certainty to win or succeed carries no real danger.

clue.text: Critic's notice sent up this old character

parts.note: Charles Lamb was an English essayist and critic

indicators.note: sent up in a down clue means the word is read upwards

parts.note: an ad is a notice

explanation.surface: A reviewer's write-up mocks this ancient figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' turns AD into DA beneath LAMB; 'this' is a link and the character is a Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The eleventh letter of the ancient Greek alphabet is an old written symbol.

clue.text: Respectful form of address reversing hard-hearted prejudice

indicators.note: hearted means the hard letter is placed at the heart of the turned word
reversing tells us the word for prejudice is turned around

parts.note: prejudice is bias
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A deferential title is used to overturn harsh bigotry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns BIAS into SAIB, and 'hearted' puts H (hard) in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A title used in colonial India for a European man or person of rank, a polite way to address him.

clue.text: Bardell, for example, in case of simple misunderstanding

parts.note: plain means simple, unadorned
a tiff is a minor quarrel

explanation.surface: Mrs Bardell is cited as the party in a lawsuit over a mere mix-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Bardell sues Mr Pickwick for breach of promise in Dickens's Pickwick Papers; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The party who brings a lawsuit is the one suing, as Mrs Bardell sued Pickwick.

clue.text: Following on to win, maybe

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of to win could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A team bats again in pursuit of victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link. A cricket team made to follow on bats again immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: Being pulled along behind something means trailing it.

clue.text: Support state party's boasting

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Backing for a state political party's bragging.
explanation.definitionFit: Swaggering show of courage, or boastful talk, is bluster.

clue.text: One conceals the party's present chances

definitions.text: One conceals the party's present chances

parts.words: One conceals the party's present chances
parts.note: a lucky dip at a children's party: gifts are buried in cereal husks and each child takes a chance

explanation.surface: Someone at a party hides the gifts and the odds of getting one.
explanation.walkthrough: A British party game: a tub filled with cereal husks hides wrapped gifts that guests dip for at random.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucky-dip tub at a fete or party, where hidden gifts are won by chance.

clue.text: Having entrance but restricted

definitions.meaning: fitted with a way in through a barrier
confined to college as a punishment, in British university slang

explanation.surface: Admitted to a place, yet limited in movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' is a link. At British universities a student so punished is kept within college bounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A road with a barred entry has one, and a student confined to college is kept in.

clue.text: Way in which crook pinches article

indicators.note: pinches means the crook word grips the article inside it

parts.note: a crook is a staff or rod
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A method by which a criminal steals an item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crook' suggests a thief but is a shepherd's staff; 'in which' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A street or route is a way.

clue.text: Diligently study course books

parts.note: a course is a direction; SW is south-west
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Someone studies hard over their textbooks for the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' looks academic but is a compass bearing; 'books' is the standard Old Testament abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for cramming hard for exams.
